articles.title: Marsh Landing Gets $850 for Basketball Court
articles.deck: The money will be spent over the next year, with the first work starting in December.
body: Public works estimates the work will take about 40 weeks once it begins.
Organizers say the project is on schedule and that volunteers are still needed on Sunday mornings.

Keith Chandler, who has lived in Marsh Landing for 40 years, said the response has been better than anyone expected. The plan calls for basketball court along Laurel Street, with work expected to start in December.

articles.title: Letter: the Mill Hill Lions Club Did a Good Job This Spring
body: To the editor: I hope the council will listen to the people who turned out at the February meeting. Please keep the stormwater drain repair in the budget. Many of us on Vernon Street use it every week.
To the editor: I have lived on Vernon Street for 24 years, and I want to say what a difference the Mill Hill Lions Club has made.
Nora Galloway, Tannery Flats

articles.deck: The vote came after 39 residents spoke at Wednesday’s session.
body: Councilmember Sadie Tiernan asked for more time to review the proposal, which would cost about $48,000.

articles.title: Talia Emerson, 72, Longtime Volunteer
articles.deck: Friends remember Talia Emerson for the many years of service to Eastgate.
body: Talia Emerson died in June at home on Juniper Lane, at the age of 72. Born in Eastgate in the years after the war, Talia Emerson spent most of a working life in the trades and most of a retirement in the neighborhood.
Services will be held at the parish hall, and donations may be made to the Cedar Hollow Garden Club in his or her name. Survivors include a daughter, two grandchildren and many friends from Eastgate.
